stem: What is a statement of the principle of conservation of momentum?

options.A: In an elastic collision, momentum is constant.
options.B: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
options.C: The force acting on a body is proportional to its rate of change of momentum.
options.D: The momentum of an isolated system is constant.

stem: In which situation is total linear momentum always conserved?

options.A: in all collisions between two objects
options.B: in collisions between two objects moving at equal and opposite velocity
options.C: in collisions between two objects that form an isolated system
options.D: in collisions between two objects with the same mass

stem:
Two objects move towards each other along the same straight line.
After colliding, the two objects stick together and are stationary.
Which statement must be correct?

options.A: The total kinetic energy of the two objects does not change during the collision.
options.B: The total momentum of the two objects before the collision is zero.
options.C: The two objects have equal mass.
options.D: The two objects have the same speed before the collision.

Two skaters push each other apart on frictionless ice. Which statement about the momentum of the two-skater system is correct?

options.A: Momentum is conserved only if the skaters have equal mass.
options.B: The total momentum stays zero, so the skaters gain equal and opposite momenta.
options.C: The total momentum increases, because each skater gains momentum.
options.D: The total momentum is conserved only if their kinetic energies are also equal.

stem: A trolley of mass 2 kg moving at 5 m s$^{-1}$ along a frictionless horizontal track collides with a stationary trolley of mass 1 kg. The trolleys stick together. Calculate their common speed immediately after the collision.

A ball of mass 3 kg moving east at 5 m s$^{-1}$ collides head-on with a ball of mass 1 kg moving west at 2 m s$^{-1}$ on a frictionless surface. The balls stick together. Calculate the speed of the combined ball immediately after the collision.

Object X, travelling at 12 m s$^{-1}$, catches up with object Y, which is moving at 3 m s$^{-1}$ in the same direction along the same straight line. The two objects have a perfectly elastic collision, and immediately afterwards X is still moving forwards at 5 m s$^{-1}$. Determine the speed of Y immediately after the collision.

A railway truck of mass 2000 kg moving at 3 m s$^{-1}$ collides with a stationary truck of mass 1000 kg on a level track. The trucks couple together. Calculate the loss of kinetic energy in the collision.

Sphere P, moving at 9.0 m s$^{-1}$, strikes a stationary sphere Q head-on. The collision is perfectly elastic and afterwards P continues forwards at 3.0 m s$^{-1}$. What is the speed of Q after the collision?
Two lumps of clay collide in an isolated system and stick together. Which row correctly describes the total momentum and the total kinetic energy of the system?

options.A: momentum not conserved, kinetic energy conserved
options.C: momentum conserved, kinetic energy not conserved
options.D: momentum not conserved, kinetic energy not conserved
